paragraphs: Five fostering services list Swindon as an area they cover, among them Swindon Borough Council's own fostering service, and they are shown above. The council says more than 300 children are in its care, and in May 2025 it said that over 100 of them live outside the borough, which is why it is asking local people to come forward so more children can stay close to home.

The council's guide to fostering says it needs carers for children from babies to teenagers, with teenagers highlighted, and for brothers and sisters who need to stay together. Alongside short and long-term fostering it offers emergency care, respite, short breaks for disabled children through its Home from Home scheme, care for unaccompanied children seeking asylum, parent and child placements, and supported lodgings for young people from 16. It says its payments start from £408 per child per week, depending on your skills and the child's needs, with an extra week's allowance for a birthday and for festivals and two extra weeks for holidays.

You need to be 21 or over, with no upper age limit, and to have a spare bedroom for children aged three and over. You can rent or own, have pets and work, and no qualifications are needed. Children under five cannot be placed with someone who smokes or vapes. Assessment involves eight to ten visits and a medical the council pays for, and the council expects it to take around six months.

Once approved you have a supervising social worker, phone support out of hours, six core courses and more training, a buddy from an experienced carer, and support groups including ones for new carers and for men who foster. Talk to the council and two or three of the services above, and see the Wiltshire, Gloucestershire and Oxfordshire pages too.
